 Inspiration 

 LearnLogos has a large collection of instructional videos, captions, and sentence-level timestamps. Learners often Blackjack remember what John taught but cannot remember the course, video, or terminology
 needed to find it. We wanted agents to retrieve LearnLogos teaching directly instead of generating a generic answer or guessing how to navigate the website. 

 ## What it does 

 The LearnLogos WebMCP Learning Assistant turns a natural-language question into the most relevant approved teaching excerpt. 

 A supported browser agent can discover and invoke learnlogos.search_training.v1 . The result includes: 

 
 The relevant lesson title and summary 
 Exact source timestamps 
 An SBL-style citation 
 An explanation of why it matched 
 Controlled video playback with captions 
 

 The visible demonstration provides eight alternative questions across two topics. Different ways of asking about program scaling find “Set Exact Program Scaling,” while reading-plan questions find “Jump to Your
 Next Reading.” 

 This demonstrates how people and agents can find the same authoritative instruction without knowing its essentially compression reti Bots exact title or location. 

 ## How we built it 

 The application uses TypeScript, Next.js, React, and Zod. The page registers a structured tool through document.modelContext.registerTool , while both the human interface and browser agent use the same
 validated search service. 

 The contest deployment is separate from the production LearnLogos website. It uses: 

 
 A hard server-side content allowlist 
 Two exact, rights-approved demonstration excerpts 
 Synthetic session state with no customer information 
 Dedicated Upstash Redis rate limiting 
 Short-lived, session-bound media grants 
 Exact media and caption digest verification 
 Same-origin restrictions and a strict content security policy 
 Automated tests covering tool registration, retrieval, authorization, media access, and browser behavior 
 

 ## Challenges 

 The largest challenge was combining a useful demonstration with strict security and intellectual-property boundaries. We needed to show real question-to-video retrieval without exposing production Nz content,
 customer data, full transcripts, or unrestricted media URLs. 

 Natural-language ranking also required care. Common words such as “the” initially created ties between unrelated lessons. We corrected this by excluding conversational filler words from ranking and added
 regression tests for every demonstration question. 

 ## What we learned 

 WebMCP works best as an interface over reusable application services—not as a separate business-logic layer. Structured tools give agents reliable inputs, validated outputs, and clear authorization boundaries
 while preserving an accessible experience for people. 

 We also learned that retrieval quality depends on preserving provenance. A useful answer should remain traceable to the exact lesson, source recording, timestamp range, and access decision. 

 ## What's next 

 The contest entry is a secure vertical slice of a larger LearnLogos vision. Future work includes searching customer-owned training first, coherent transcript segmentation, hybrid semantic retrieval,
 personalized learning paths, progress-aware recommendations, and secure previews of additional approved lessons. 

 LearnLogos is an independent training provider. It is not owned, operated, sponsored, or endorsed by Logos.
